A points failure has been reported near Downham Market, preventing trains from travelling through this area.
Points are movable sections of track that allow trains to change routes at junctions. If they develop a fault, they may not move into the correct position or the signalling system may be unable to confirm they are securely positioned. Sometimes, points can be secured in one position to allow some trains to continue. However, in this case, they cannot be safely secured in a position that allows trains to run, so the routes must remain closed.

Points are movable sections of track that allow trains to change routes at junctions. If they develop a fault, they may not move into the correct position or the signalling system may be unable to confirm they are securely positioned. Sometimes, points can be secured in one position to allow some trains to continue. Points are movable sections of track that allow trains to change routes at junctions. nrIncident.message:
Lines have reopened following a fault with fault with the signalling system between Berwick-upon-Tweed and Newcastle.
Whilst service recovers, trains running between these stations may be cancelled in full, delayed by up to 45 minutes or revised to only run for part of their normal journey.
If you have an LNER, Lumo or TransPennine Express ticket dated for travel yesterday, Sunday 15 November, and you deferred travel, you will be able to use your ticket to travel today, Monday 16 November, at no extra cost. LNER customers only may also use their tickets on Tuesday 17 and Wednesday 18 November.
Disruption is expected until 15:30.
There are a number of different options available to help you complete your journey. Please check your whole journey using the National Rail Enquiries journey planner as some of the alternative routes listed below that you can use your ticket on may also be affected by this disruption.
LNER customer advice:
Rail replacement services are on standby at Newcastle.
You can use the alternative route map to help you with your journey. Please be aware that other operators' services are likely to be busy.
TransPennine Express customer advice:
You may use your ticket to travel on the following services at no extra cost:
• Alternative TransPennine Express services between Edinburgh and Carlisle
• Avanti West Coast services between Edinburgh and Carlisle
• Northern services between Newcastle and Carlisle
Customers at / for East Linton, Dunbar, Reston, Berwick-upon-Tweed, Alnmouth and Morpeth should see station staff or use station help points where onward travel advice will be provided.
Ticket flexibility:
If your train is cancelled, you will be able to travel on an alternative service operated by any other participating train company, either two hours before or two hours after the original departure time of the cancelled service, in order to reach your destination.
If you decide not to travel or cannot complete your journey due to cancellations, you are entitled to a full refund from your original point of sale.
For further information and guidance please contact your train company or speak to a member of railway staff.
Check before you travel:
You can check your journey using the National Rail real-time Journey Planner.
For helpful advice if you need to travel on a rail replacement service, including accessibility and bicycle information, please use our Rail Replacement Services page.
You can find the pick-up and drop-off location of rail replacement services by checking station signage or by searching for your station on our Find a Station page.
Please be advised that replacement vehicles may be busier than usual, and you should allow extra time for your journey.
Compensation:
You may be entitled to compensation if you experience a delay in completing your journey today. Please keep your train ticket and make a note of your journey, as both will be required to support any claim.
